decisions.quote: Call et al. (2013) described a method of assessing the function of social interactions that used time allocation as a dependent measure. The current study replicated the method described by Call et al. and evaluated several extensions aimed at increasing the feasibility and efficiency of the assessment and the utility of its results. Seven children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) participated. Social interactions were concluded to be reinforcing for 5 participants and aversive for 2 partcipants.
decisions.reason: The supplied abstract states that the study replicated the method of Call et al. (2013) with extensions and reports participant results, but does not state how those results compare to Call et al.'s original findings. Because only the abstract is available, it neither confirms 'successful' nor establishes the absence of a comparison to the original findings in the unseen full text as required for 'descriptive only'.

parent_objection: Codebook descriptive only applies only where authors themselves say they applied original methods in a new context/population; example1 uses method replication with no original claim test. Supplied abstract says Call2013 described a method and current study replicated that method in7ASDchildren and evaluated methodological extensions. First reply withholds descriptive only solely because full text might contain comparisons. Does the authors own methods-use framing establish descriptive only from available source, rather than an unsupported absence inference? Conversely, is a specific original substantive finding actually stated and compared? Apply exact codebook without requiring unseen evidence to rule out every possible comparison.
